ex-201-1.title: Calculating displacement
ex-201-1.question:
A car travels from A to B along the path as shown.

(a) Find the total distance travelled by the car.

(b) Find the total displacement of the car.
ex-201-1.answer:
(a) Total distance travelled

= 1 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 1

= 9 km

(b) Magnitude:

AB = 22 + 52 = 5.39 km

Direction:

tan θ = 52

θ = 68.2°

The total displacement is 5.39 km (N68.2°E).
ex-201-1.think: If another car travels from A to B such that its distance travelled is equal to the magnitude of its total displacement, what would its path be?
ex-201-1.thinkAnswer: It must travel directly along the straight line from A to B without reversing direction. The distance is then the length AB, 5.39 km, in the direction N68.2°E.

ex-201-2.title: Average speed and speed limit
ex-201-2.question:
A car travels 7.2 km in 10 minutes.

(a) Find the average speed of the car. Give your answer in km h−1.

(b) The speed limit on the road is 80 km h−1. According to the answer in

(a), can we conclude that the driver obeys the speed limit?
ex-201-2.tips:
Tip

Time in min should be converted to time in h:

10 min = 1060 h

Tip

According to the information given, we are not sure whether the instantaneous speed of the car at any instant exceeds the speed limit.

ex-201-3.title: Average speed and average velocity
ex-201-3.question:
A bicycle travels 800 m north and then 600 m west in 400 s.

(a) Find its average speed.

(b) Find its average velocity.
ex-201-3.answer:
(a) Average speed = dt

= 800 + 600400

= 3.5 m s−1

(b) Magnitude:

Magnitude of total displacement = 8002 + 6002 = 1000 m

Magnitude of average velocity = st = 1000400 = 2.5 m s−1

Direction:

tan θ = 600800

θ = 36.9°

The average velocity is 2.5 m s−1 (N36.9°W).
ex-201-3.tips:
Skill

Problem-solving

Finding average velocity Follow the steps below to find the average velocity. ① Draw the path of the object. ② Draw the total displacement (an arrow from the initial position to the final position). ③ Find the magnitude and direction of the average velocity.

ex-201-4.title: Uniform motion
ex-201-4.question:
The positions of object X (represented by •) and Y (represented by ×) at

time t = 0, 1 s, 2 s and 3 s are as shown.

One of the objects is in uniform motion. Which one is it? Explain briefly.
ex-201-4.answer: X is in uniform motion as its velocity is constant.
ex-201-4.tips:
Tip

The distance travelled by X in each second remains the same and it keeps moving in the same direction. On the other hand, the distance travelled by Y in each second increases, showing that it accelerates.

ex-201-5.title: Percentage error in timing
ex-201-5.question:
Polly wants to use a stop-watch to find out the time T for a swing to move one cycle.

(a) Polly uses the stop-watch to measure the time for the swing to move one cycle directly. Her result is 2.31 s. If the error due to reaction time is 0.4 s, what is the percentage error due to reaction time?

(b) She then uses the stop-watch to measure the time for the swing to move 10 cycles and the result is 22.48 s. The erroe due to reaction time is still 0.4 s.

(i) What is the value of T according to this measurement?

(ii) What is the percentage error due to her reaction time in this measurement?

ex-201-6.title: Percentage error in measurement
ex-201-6.question: Patrick measures the length of an object. His result is 19.1 cm, with an uncertainty of ±0.1 cm. What is the maximum percentage error in Patrick’s measurement?
ex-201-6.tips:
Tip

The absolute value of the uncertainty of a measurement gives the maximum error.

ex-201-7.title: Reducing percentage error
ex-201-7.question:
A line of 9 light dots is produced in an experiment. The dots are evenly spaced by a distance x. John and Mary want to measure the value of x.

(a) John uses a ruler to measure the distance between 2 dots directly. His result is 4 mm, with an uncertainty of ±1 mm. What is the maximum percentage error in this measurement?

(b) Mary uses the same ruler to measure the distance between the first dot and the last dot. Her result is 30 mm, with an uncertainty of ±1 mm.

(i) What is the value of x according to Mary’s measurement?

(ii) What is the maximum percentage error in this measurement?

(iii) What is the maximum error in x according to Mary’s measurement?

(c) Who obtains a more accurate value of x?
ex-201-7.answer:
(a) Maximum percentage error = 14 × 100% = 25%

(b) (i) x = 308 = 3.75 mm

(ii) Maximum percentage error = 130 × 100% = 3.33%

(iii) Maximum error in x = 3.75 × 3.33% = 0.125 mm

(c) Mary
ex-201-7.tips:
Skill

Experiment

Error in measurement All measurements carry errors. To show how significant an error is in a measurement, we should consider the percentage error instead of the size of the error. The smaller the percentage error, the more accurate the measured value.

Tip

The maximum percentage error in x is the same as that in the measurement.
